headline: Customers can now stack promo codes, but nothing limits it, so anyone can get a free order by entering codes repeatedly.
what_changed: The checkout used to allow only one promo code per order. It now accepts any number of codes on the same order.
The discounts are added together. For example, the referral code (15% off) plus the spring code (25% off) now gives 40% off.
The same code can be entered more than once, and each entry adds its discount again. This was not part of the stated goal.
The code note says the aim was to let a referral code combine with a seasonal promo. The change allows much more than that: any code combines with any other, including the staff code.
One new automatic test was added to check that the referral and spring codes combine correctly.

risks.title: Entering the same code repeatedly gives free orders
risks.explanation: Nothing stops a customer from entering the same code again and again. Entering the spring code four times takes 100% off. The payment step treats a zero or negative total as a free order and charges nothing. Any customer who tries this gets goods for free. Fix: reject a code that is already on the order, and never let the discount go above the order price.

risks.title: No cap on combined discounts across different codes
risks.explanation: Every code can be stacked with every other code, with no limit on the total. The four current codes together give exactly 100% off, which again means a free order. The staff 50% code can also be combined with customer codes. Fix: allow only the pairing you actually want (one referral code plus one seasonal code), and cap the total discount.

risks.title: Order total can go below zero
risks.explanation: Because discounts are simply added up, the final price can become negative, not just zero. Today this produces a free order rather than a refund. But any receipt, invoice or report that reads this total could show a negative price. The fix above (capping the discount at the order price) solves this too.

questions_for_developer: Which codes should be allowed to combine? Was the plan only one referral code plus one seasonal code, or any codes at all?
Can you block a code that is already on the order, and make sure the total discount can never go above the order price?
Should the staff discount code ever combine with customer codes? If not, can you block that?
Can you add tests that try to apply the same code twice and try stacking all codes, to prove these lead to a sensible price rather than a free order?
good_news: The change is small and only touches the discount part of the cart, so fixing it should be quick.
Invalid codes are still rejected, and the existing tests were updated to match the new behaviour.
